commits.edited_message: ttvarc.c: Improve offset validation and axis-buffer capacity.

coupling: The first edited commit raises the semantic VARC axis-value stack limit from 64 to 128; both the array and the capacity passed to the parser grow together, so that commit is safe alone. The later edited commit introduces a distinct physical axis-buffer capacity of 64 and sizes stack_axis_values with it, while the parser still receives VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT as its capacity. After the first commit that reported capacity is 128, so a public FT_Load_Glyph input containing 65 axis values takes the stack path and writes one FT_Fixed past the 64-entry array. With only the first edit, array and reported capacity are both 128; with only the second edit, both are 64. A correct repair must reconcile the semantic limit, physical array capacity, and capacity reported to the parser across the two maintenance changes rather than treating either constant in isolation.
